# sources/test-tools/syzkaller/pkg/report/testdata/linux/report/51

Purpose: Linux reporter parse fixture for syzkaller. It encodes the expected parsed title `memory leak in do_ipv6_setsockopt`, expected type `LEAK`, alternate titles `none`, corrupted flag `N`, and panicked flag `N`. The source is a static kernel-console transcript, not executable test code; its job is to pin how the Linux reporter recognizes kmemleak allocation leak detection. It has no explicit `REPORT:` block, so the parser derives the report from the console transcript and expected headers.

Important APIs, types, and functions: this file is consumed by `pkg/report/report_test.go` through `testParseImpl`, `Reporter.ContainsCrash`, `Reporter.Parse`, and `Reporter.ParseFrom`. It exercises Linux reporter pattern tables and title extraction in `linux.go`, generic report shaping in `report.go`, and crash-type mapping through `pkg/report/crash.TitleToType`. Parser-relevant functions and symbols visible in the complete log include `sock_kmalloc`, `ipv6_setsockopt`, `sctp_setsockopt`, `sock_common_setsockopt`, `SyS_setsockopt`. Diagnostic tokens visible in the complete fixture include BUG, memory leak.

Control flow: the test harness enumerates `pkg/report/testdata/linux/report`, reads expectation headers until the blank line or `REPORT:` marker, and feeds the remaining bytes to a Linux `Reporter`. For this fixture, `ContainsCrash` must match the expected crash, `Parse` must locate the first report span, and `ParseFrom` must rediscover the same crash from its start offset but not after its end offset. The log-specific flow is: kmemleak output records an unreferenced allocation whose allocation stack reaches `do_ipv6_setsockopt`, making the leak title depend on the allocation call chain. There are 16 source lines; exact report-body comparison is `no`.

State and persistence behavior: all persistent state lives in this text file: header expectations, alternate titles, crash transcript bytes, and any explicit report body. During tests, state is transient parser output: crash start/end offsets, selected title, alternate titles, crash type, corruption/panic flags, guilty-file hints, and trimmed report bytes. The fixture performs no filesystem, network, device, or kernel mutation; it models those kernel-side events only as immutable input text.

Dependencies and integration points: the fixture integrates with syzkaller's Linux report recognizer, stack-frame skip lists, sanitizer parsers, lockdep/warning/hung-task detectors, panic handling, corruption handling, and report-boundary logic. Product-level consumers are crash deduplication, dashboard grouping, repro triage, maintainer signal routing, and automated bisection. Because the source lives under `testdata/linux/report`, its filename is intentionally opaque; the headers and transcript are the behavioral contract.

Risks and edge cases: short kmemleak fixtures have little context, so leak classification depends on preserving the allocation stack and not treating the leading `BUG` text as a kernel BUG. More generally, regressions can come from overfitting to timestamps, CPU/task prefixes, architecture-specific syscall wrappers, compiler suffixes such as `.cold`, `.part`, or `.constprop`, repeated helper frames, panic-on-warn trailers, allocation/free stacks, or noisy subsystem messages preceding the crash. Reports flagged as corrupted must remain conservative about title specificity, while non-crash logs must not be promoted just because they contain alarming words.

Test signals: a passing parser run returns title `memory leak in do_ipv6_setsockopt`, type `LEAK`, alternate titles `none`, corrupted `N`, panicked `N`, and exact-body comparison `no`. It must keep the meaningful frame named by the expected title when the log provides one, avoid helper-only titles, preserve panic/corruption semantics, and produce stable output across `Parse` and `ParseFrom`.
